chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his fathers (peace be upon them) that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
"When one of you finishes the prayer, let him raise his hands to the sky and stand erect in supplication."
Ibn Sab' said: O Amir al-Mu'minin, is not Allah in every place? He said: "Yes."
He said: Then why does he raise his hands to the sky? He said: "Do you not read in the Quran: 'And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised'"
And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised
So from where is provision sought except from its place? And the place of provision and what Allah promised is the sky."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims raise their hands to the sky during dua according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the wisdom behind raising hands to the sky during *dua*, addressing the apparent paradox of God's omnipresence. He cites the verse regarding provision being in the heavens to establish the sky as the symbolic locus (*majaz*) for seeking sustenance, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a sign of humility and expectation.
